## Requirement acceptance and evidence

| Requirement | Acceptance criteria | Status | Evidence | Open finding |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `REQ-001` | The release inventory and acceptance evidence contain functioning deliverables for all four areas and both reasoning modes; a roadmap, design, mockup, or disconnected prototype does not replace any required capability., Optional installation or activation of a backend means a configurable delivered feature, not permission to omit its implementation or acceptance. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-002` | Existing valid records and core commands remain compatible; added semantic profiles and fields have explicit versions and capabilities, and unsupported older readers fail clearly rather than misinterpret them., No automatic memory or Task schema migration, concept-ID recycling, core-ID redefinition, or child-project adoption occurs., Acceptance of integration requires evidence that the applicable first-release foundation works; the first TRD's trd_done status alone does not prove implementation. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-003` | Core lookup, validation, and wiki generation operate with all advanced profiles absent or disabled; enabled advanced operations report missing or incompatible dependencies without claiming success., Installation, model preparation, service startup, and profile upgrades occur only through separately selected setup operations; a query or document approval performs none of them., Profiles report their exact runtime/package/model versions and input compatibility; RDFLib and pySHACL remain the report-derived standards-backend basis, with exact versions selected and tested during planning. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-004` | Remote JSON-LD contexts, unselected OWL imports, escaping paths, symlinks, external XML resources, and federated query targets cannot cause unauthorized reads or network requests., Uploaded ontology content cannot enable executable extensions, plugins, JavaScript, Python code, or custom query functions; supported extensions are explicitly registered project capabilities., Tests observe prohibited access attempts being blocked, rather than relying only on a denylist of literal strings or a documentation warning. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-005` | The adapter exposes separately identifiable graph contexts for the included fact classes and records exact canonical inputs, module versions, configuration, and adapter version., Materializing or querying the RDF projection does not make it an alternative authoring store or change canonical ontology bytes., Only selected, permitted project modules and bindings enter the dataset; a cross-system link does not import another project's graph automatically. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-006` | Export followed by staged re-import preserves the supported identities, typed values, relations, and graph membership; semantic equivalence accounts for serialization order and blank-node renaming., A graph-only export identifies its selected graph and supplies a companion context/provenance manifest or explicitly rejects an unsupported lossless export; it never silently flattens distinct fact classes., Imported data is validated and staged as an attributed proposal, with namespace conflicts and unsupported constructs reported before any canonical publication., Export destinations and overwrite behavior are explicit; imports cannot overwrite canonical content or grant trust merely because their syntax is valid. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-007` | A result can be traced to the exact source entity and the activity that produced it; available producer attribution and derivation links survive export., Provenance identifies evidence and production history, not execution permission or approval of a proposal., Changed or missing evidence is visible as stale or unavailable rather than represented as verified current provenance. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-008` | Representative queries return tabular bindings, a Boolean answer, or a result graph as appropriate, with project/dataset identity, versions, and whether asserted or inferred graphs were selected., Named-graph selection is explicit; graph-producing queries return results without inserting them into canonical or persistent stores., Supported DESCRIBE behavior, result ordering, and nondeterministic expressions are documented; repeatability checks use a defined deterministic query/result profile. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-009` | Update operations and SERVICE federation are rejected; FROM and FROM NAMED can select only already permitted local dataset graphs and cannot trigger retrieval of external resources., Malformed, prohibited, cancelled, or resource-limited queries return distinct diagnostics; partial results are not labeled complete., Query execution changes no canonical or generated persistent state, and cannot silently install a backend or refresh an index. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-010` | Shapes cover required definitions/provenance, identity references, relation endpoint types, and configured cardinalities; overlap with core checks yields compatible results., Reports distinguish conformance, violations, and inability to complete validation, and identify the affected entity, path, shape, severity, and useful diagnostic., Invalid shapes, unsupported features, missing backends, and processing errors cannot become a passing validation or an execution authorization., Validation identifies its graph scope and whether inference was applied; inferred triples cannot supply missing approval/provenance or bypass the core authoring checks. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-011` | Approved rules and example facts yield the expected additional types or relationships, including a generated wiki page being recognized as an Artifact through its declared type hierarchy., The supported reasoning profile and its limits are explicit; required competency cases determine profile adequacy, and unsupported axioms are reported rather than silently ignored., Draft proposals and merely similar labels do not enter the approved reasoning premises; identity equivalence requires an approved semantic assertion. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-012` | An agent and a human can distinguish authored assertions, inferred conclusions, and AI suggestions and inspect the premise/rule chain for a selected inferred result., Rebuilding or discarding inference results changes no canonical assertion or historical memory; accepting a proposed semantic change still requires publication., A reasoning pass never grants Task, role, tool, or publication authority. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-013` | An absent relationship is not automatically treated as false or as a permission denial/approval unless an explicit applicable constraint defines that interpretation., Inconsistent approved premises produce an actionable conflict report; unrelated conclusions are not presented as trustworthy merely because the engine completed., Validation and authorization decisions use their own explicit rules rather than treating incomplete inference as proof of compliance. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-014` | Limit exhaustion, cancellation, unsupported semantics, and stale input return clear non-success states; no incomplete closure is silently labeled complete., Identical pinned inputs produce equivalent conclusions and stable normalized evidence; changing a premise invalidates dependent results., Live recomputation does not replace the ontology packet already frozen for an active solver round. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-015` | An authorized agent/model run produces a concrete structured proposal from an identified source packet, with supporting references, rationale, affected identities, and explicit uncertainty., Instructions embedded in sources remain data; generated content cannot expand read/write scope, invoke actions, or approve itself., Generation uses an explicitly permitted runtime and source scope; it does not silently provision a model, request credentials, or send project data to a new service. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-016` | A proposal displays its evidence, semantic diff, generator attribution, current review state, and any superseding revision; unsupported claims are visible., Revising or regenerating a proposal preserves its earlier review history and invalidates approvals tied to obsolete content., AI generation need not be byte-deterministic; review, validation, and publication bind the exact captured candidate bytes. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-017` | Candidate checks run without publishing the proposal or contaminating approved retrieval; reports identify regressions, conflicts, unsupported semantics, and source freshness., A candidate cannot become eligible merely because an LLM endorses it or because it passes syntax validation., Reviewers can inspect the affected definitions, relations, generated wiki/query results, and downstream semantic effects before accepting exact content. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-018` | Approval binds the exact current proposal and target hashes; stale evidence, changed targets, missing grants, or conflicting ownership prevent publication., Accept, reject, revise, and supersede have distinct recorded outcomes; rejecting or discarding a proposal changes no approved ontology., An approved edit becomes canonical only when its actual publication receipt and reopened target bytes establish success; partial failure reports its real committed boundary. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-019` | A revised proposal addresses named findings and retains source/version lineage; unchanged failures or exhausted limits stop with unresolved findings., Evaluation shows whether the candidate improves the relevant competency behavior and reports regressions or lack of benefit without requiring a predetermined improvement percentage., Training or self-modification of the agent is not required to perform this proposal-refinement workflow. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-020` | With the profile enabled, an otherwise missed paraphrase can return a sourced ontology concept labeled as a semantic match; it does not displace an exact identity match., Model/index/input versions and stale-index status are visible; absence of the profile preserves first-release lexical and graph retrieval., Embedding similarity does not establish semantic equivalence, approve a new concept, or access sources excluded from the selected project or frozen packet. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-021` | The comparison records the dataset, ontology/configuration/model versions, expected facts and sources, retrieval correctness, attribution, resource use, and observed failures., An automatically extracted graph remains exploratory or proposed knowledge; it is not promoted to normative project vocabulary by the evaluation., The report's published study percentages are not treated as guaranteed Sys4AI outcomes; useful negative or neutral results remain valid evidence. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-022` | Coverage includes applicable ontology and memory publication, Task lifecycle/ownership operations, TRD/plan lifecycle operations, role/asset changes, and project setup/adoption through their supported project interfaces., Every covered operation resolves to a current action contract and dispatch binding; missing, stale, and unsupported bindings are reported explicitly., Action contracts describe semantic validity and capability; current user/role/Task authority still determines whether the actor may act. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-023` | A semantically invalid covered request reaches no underlying mutation helper; a valid request proceeds only after the existing authorization checks succeed., Guarding is demonstrated through actual dispatch adapters, not only an independently callable validator that callers may accidentally omit., Coverage diagnostics distinguish guarded project paths from direct host/third-party paths outside the integration; the system makes no unsupported claim of intercepting every native tool or shell command. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-024` | Each failure returns its action identity, failing condition, relevant source/version, and an actionable diagnostic without invoking the requested side effect., A timeout, unknown result, or backend failure cannot be converted to a pass, and retry does not silently disable the guard., An explicitly disabled guard profile is reported as disabled; existing authorization checks remain active and no disabled path is advertised as semantically protected. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-025` | Changing arguments, a target revision, an ontology rule, governing source, manager generation, or approval scope invalidates the old decision., Tests exercise a change between preview/check and dispatch; a stale pass cannot authorize the new operation., The integration respects existing helper transactions and locks, reports real consistency limits, and does not fabricate a cross-system atomicity guarantee. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-026` | A successful record identifies the checked request, decision versions, authoritative authorization outcome, actual helper receipt, and verified target result., Semantic success without authorization or execution is reported only as semantic success; errors and partial mutations retain their true status., Logs and durable receipts contain bounded operational evidence without credentials, unnecessary personal data, hidden reasoning, or full transcripts. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-027` | A user can find a concept by ID, label, or alias; inspect incoming/outgoing relations; filter by module, type, lifecycle, or fact classification; and navigate to its source evidence., Approved assertions, inferred facts, imported material, and AI proposals remain visually distinguishable, with a readable list/inspector alternative to the graph., The workbench reports the selected project and current readiness accurately and does not require a hosted website or remote service for basic browsing. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-028` | An author can add a concept and relationship, edit their supported fields, validate the draft, and inspect the resulting semantic diff without hand-editing JSON., Imported locked core content is protected; project extensions and distinct replacement identities follow existing rules rather than silently redefining an imported ID., Deprecation/replacement preserves historical IDs, while unsupported destructive changes are rejected or routed through their separately authorized lifecycle. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-029` | A user can inspect an AI proposal's evidence and validation results, revise or reject it, and publish only when the actual current project authority permits the exact operation., Draft saving, successful validation, and clicking a review control do not themselves approve or publish canonical semantics., After publication, the workbench reopens the canonical result and shows its real status and receipt; it does not declare success from a queued request alone. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-030` | Two clients editing the same target cannot silently overwrite each other; a stale save or publish reports the conflict and retains the draft for review., Cancel, discard, and failed validation leave approved content unchanged; a partial publication shows exactly what committed and what remains unresolved., Reloading or reopening a saved draft preserves its identity, content, evidence, and review state. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-031` | A user can complete search, draft editing, validation, diff review, and the permitted publication/rejection flow without relying on graph dragging or color alone., Field errors identify what failed and preserve entered content; loading, unavailable profiles, stale results, and partial failures have distinct visible states., The main flow explains concepts and review consequences without exposing unnecessary implementation details. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-032` | The default listener is restricted to the local machine; remotely exposing it requires a separate selected deployment and access policy., Forged actor fields, stale review tokens, unauthorized browser origins/requests, escaping file paths, and executable content in labels/imports do not cause unauthorized reads, writes, or script execution., Browser controls use the same guarded publication/validation interfaces as other supported clients and retain their exact target/version checks. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-033` | The current manager freezes exact packet bytes before dispatch and supplies identical references to every independent initial solver, including queued solvers., Further queries cannot add live facts, new AI proposals, new embeddings/documents, changed rules, or sibling/current-execution candidate material outside the permitted frozen inputs., The packet uses existing path/SHA256 interfaces and size limits; selection/truncation is explicit and no new Task schema field or ownership route is introduced. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-034` | A newly published concept or rule does not silently enter active solver context; the manager assesses its effect and repeats the existing affected input/review/acceptance gates when material., Execution guards check current approved action context and reject an action based on stale inputs without rewriting the solver's frozen packet., Ontology integration neither replaces the current Task manager nor changes required team composition, role authority, or lifecycle status. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-035` | Ontology inference, proposal publication, visual editing, and RDF import/export do not rewrite existing memory records or add unsupported fields., Advanced mixed queries retain the identities and source types of definitions, inferences, proposals, and historical evidence and cannot upgrade memory into operational authority., Memory-side mutations occur only through their own authorized operations; new semantic links remain derived and versioned. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-036` | The root installation exposes and verifies all four capability areas against current root bindings, with exact versions and readiness for the selected profiles., Reusable assets contain no root project instances, proposal history, credentials, generated indexes, or runtime state., Adoption preserves unrelated local files and existing approvals/authority; any needed governance-binding refresh is exact, scoped, and verified rather than inferred from file similarity. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-037` | New/first-prepared projects receive their own identity, locked core/extension versions, and empty project data; backend/model activation and publication authority are destination-local and accurately reported., Existing projects and prior receipt editions retain their content, configuration, imports, licenses, memory choices, and provenance until an exact adoption/upgrade is selected., Customized or incompatible packages are preserved and diagnosed; upgrades and recovery use current expected versions and the existing receipt model, with no bulk product propagation. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-038` | A maintainer can enable an authorized profile, run inference/SPARQL/SHACL, generate and review a proposal, visually edit a draft, and understand a rejected action using the delivered instructions., Captured drafts/proposals, approvals, and publication/recovery receipts remain durable; rebuilding graphs or indexes cannot delete that accepted work., Documentation and health output distinguish implemented, installed, enabled, validated, guarded, and unexercised capabilities, and report limitations without advertising unsupported behavior. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-039` | Tests cover graph/dataset round trips, typed/language-tagged literals, source/provenance retention, all supported query forms, shape conformance, violations, and validation failure., Tests observe rejection of SPARQL updates, SERVICE, remote contexts/imports, external XML resources, escaping paths, untrusted executable extensions, and resource-limit violations., Actual results identify dependency/profile/input versions; successful core-only tests or mocked backend outputs cannot prove this requirement. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-040` | Cases show a correct inferred type and property relationship with inspectable premises/rules, an unproven conclusion that remains unproven, and an inconsistent or unsupported case that does not pass as valid., Changing an approved premise invalidates its dependent result; a bounded/cancelled run reports incomplete reasoning accurately., Captured outputs prove engine behavior and versioned evidence rather than relying on an LLM's prose explanation of what the engine should do. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-041` | An actual authorized model/agent run generates a sourced candidate; a supported change can be reviewed and published through the normal gate, while unsupported or conflicting content remains unapproved., Evaluation includes changed evidence, stale approval, attempted instruction injection, and a revision responding to a concrete validation finding., Prewritten candidates or parser tests alone do not establish proposal-generation capability; missing runtime evidence remains explicitly unverified. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-042` | The coverage report maps each supported action family and dispatch path to observed tests; negative cases prove that the underlying side effect was not invoked., At least one valid authorized action reaches its owning helper and its result is reopened; semantic success without authority is rejected., Input changes between preview and execution invalidate the earlier pass, and execution/partial failure receipts retain truthful status., Any uncovered host or direct bypass path is disclosed as outside observed coverage rather than described as protected. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-043` | A browser session searches and inspects a concept, explores a relation/derivation, edits a draft, observes a validation error, reviews a diff, publishes an authorized change, and reopens its canonical result., Separate cases verify rejected/unauthorized publication, concurrent-edit conflict, draft preservation, keyboard operation, and readable non-graph access., A static screenshot, mockup, or frontend-only fixture does not establish end-to-end editing or publication. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-044` | The combined flow resolves a concept, derives a fact with provenance, uses advanced retrieval where selected, generates and reviews a proposal, and applies an authorized visual change through a semantic guard., Representative independent solver assignments receive the same advanced packet digest; post-dispatch ontology changes follow reassessment without silent context replacement., Before/after checks prove canonical memory preservation, project isolation, no unintended product adoption, and continued core operation with advanced profiles disabled., Release acceptance supplies current evidence for each required capability and interface; unavailable prerequisites or unexercised integration remain incomplete rather than being replaced by a smaller demonstration. | `active` | 0 | None |
